statement: QLEADER must create a legacy leader with annotation, prompting for leader points (limited by the Number of Points setting), text width, tolerance frame or block insertion according to the Leader Settings dialog, and support associative arrowheads under DIMASSOC.

acceptance.sketch: Run QLEADER with Settings set to MText and 3 points, pick three points and enter text 'NOTE'; a leader with two segments and mtext 'NOTE' at its end is created.

notes: Added from help page "QLEADER (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Leaders must be a line or spline with an arrowhead and an attached multiline text or block (with optional landing), remain associated to the object snapped by the arrowhead so that the landing stretches when that object moves, and lose association in the documented cases such as block redefinition.

acceptance.sketch: Create a leader whose arrowhead is snapped to a line endpoint, move the line, and assert the arrowhead follows and the landing stretches; redefine the block so the attachment moves and assert the association is dropped.

notes: Added from help page "About Leader Objects"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Multileader creation must support straight or spline leaders built starting from the arrowhead, the tail or the content, from a multileader style, with several leader lines and segments per note, editing via MLEADEREDIT or grip menus, and per-scale annotative head points, landing sizes and gaps.

acceptance.sketch: Create a multileader with two leader lines to one note, add a third with MLEADEREDIT and assert three leader lines share the note; switch annotation scale and assert head points differ per scale.

notes: Added from help page "About Creating Leaders"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Multileader styles must define landing, leader line, arrowhead and content formatting (a default STANDARD style with straight line, closed filled arrow and mtext), be settable as current for MLEADER, and be applicable to existing leaders; annotative blocks are not allowed as content or arrowheads.

acceptance.sketch: Define a style with a spline leader and a dot arrowhead, set it current, run MLEADER and assert the new leader uses it; assign an annotative block as arrowhead and assert it is rejected.

notes: Added from help page "About Leader Styles"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Selected multileaders must expose multi-functional grips: leader endpoint (stretch, add vertex, remove leader), landing-end vertex (stretch, lengthen landing, add leader) and intermediate vertex (stretch, add or remove vertex).

acceptance.sketch: Select a multileader, use the landing-end grip's Add Leader to add a second leader line and assert the object has two; use Remove Vertex on a middle vertex and assert the vertex count drops by one.

notes: Added from help page "About Modifying Leaders With Grips"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The dimensioning system must create linear (horizontal, vertical, aligned, rotated), arc-length, ordinate, angular and radial types, with the DIM command choosing the type from the picked object and position, driven by dimension styles.

acceptance.sketch: Run DIM on a horizontal line and place the text above it and assert a horizontal linear dimension is created; run DIM on a circle and assert a radius dimension is created.

notes: Added from help page "About the Types of Dimensions"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Dimension scale (DIMSCALE) must multiply sizes and offsets such as text height, arrowhead size and extension origin offset but not measured values or tolerances, support the model-space, paper-space and viewport dimensioning workflows, and annotative dimensions must follow the current annotation scale.

acceptance.sketch: Set DIMSCALE=2 with text height 2.5 and assert drawn text is 5 units tall while the measured value is unchanged; create an annotative dimension and change annotation scale to see its size change.

notes: Added from help page "About Setting the Scale for Dimensions"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: A dimension style must be a named set of dimension settings (arrowheads, text placement, tolerances and so on) that newly created dimensions use, that updates every dimension referencing it when changed, and that supports substyles per dimension type and overrides.

acceptance.sketch: Create a style with 3-unit arrowheads, make a dimension with it, edit the style to 5 units and assert the existing dimension updates; add a radial substyle and assert only radial dimensions change.

notes: Added from help page "About Dimension Styles"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Users must be able to modify styles or change the current one, choose whether existing dimensions update, restore a style or apply the current style (with overrides) to selected dimensions, and baseline or continued dimensions inherit their parent's style unless DIMCONTINUEMODE says otherwise.

acceptance.sketch: Create a dimension, switch current style, run the Update/apply action on it and assert it adopts the new style; with DIMCONTINUEMODE off assert a continued dimension keeps its parent's style.

notes: Added from help page "About Applying Dimension Styles"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must list dimension styles (distinguishing xref-dependent ones shown as Xref: drawing name), list all dimension variables or only style-controlled ones including running overrides, and compare a named style against the current one.

acceptance.sketch: Compare two styles that differ only in arrowhead size and assert the report lists just that setting; attach an xref with a dimension style and assert it appears under the xref name.

notes: Added from help page "About Comparing Dimension Styles"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Dimension style overrides must temporarily change settings either on the current style (applied to every new dimension until deleted, saved as a new style or another style is made current) or on individual dimensions, without altering the underlying style.

acceptance.sketch: Override extension line color to red on the current style, create two dimensions and assert both are red while the saved style is unchanged; set another style current and assert new dimensions are not red.

notes: Added from help page "About Overriding a Dimension Style"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Dimensions must be editable with editing commands and grips, staying associated with their geometry when both are edited in one command, and automatically becoming disassociated in the documented cases such as erase, Boolean operations, grip-stretching parallel to the dimension line, or a vanished apparent intersection.

acceptance.sketch: Move a line and its dimension together and assert the dimension stays associative and updates; erase the line and assert the dimension is disassociated.

notes: Added from help page "About Modifying Dimension Geometry"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Dimension text must be movable (left, right, centered, anywhere between or beyond the extension lines, or returned to the style-defined home position), rotatable and replaceable, with text grips offering stretch and related options and vertical alignment preserved when moved.

acceptance.sketch: Move the text of a linear dimension with its grip and assert the dimension line adjusts; use Home Text and assert the text returns to the style-defined position.

notes: Added from help page "About Modifying Dimension Text"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: DIMSPACE must evenly space or align (spacing 0) selected parallel linear or concentric angular dimensions of the same type that lie on each other's extension lines, independent of later DIMDLI changes.

acceptance.sketch: Select three linear dimensions with uneven offsets, run DIMSPACE with value 10 and assert baselines are exactly 10 apart; run with 0 and assert dimension lines are collinear.

notes: Added from help page "About Adjusting the Spacing Between Dimensions"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: DIMBREAK must add automatic or manual breaks to dimension, extension and leader lines of linear, angular, radial, arc length, ordinate dimensions and straight multileaders where cutting-edge objects cross them, and remove all breaks via a Remove option.

acceptance.sketch: Cross a linear dimension's extension line with a line, run DIMBREAK Auto and assert a gap appears; run Remove and assert all breaks vanish.

notes: Added from help page "About Creating Breaks in Dimensions"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Any dimension must be convertible to an inspection dimension with a frame of two parallel lines (round or square ends) and up to three fields separated by vertical lines: a label, the measured value and a check rate.

acceptance.sketch: Run DIMINSPECT on a linear dimension with label 'A1', round ends and rate 100% and assert the frame displays three sections with those values.

notes: Added from help page "About Converting Dimensions Into Inspection Dimensions"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must create associative center marks for circles and arcs and centerlines between two selected lines (using apparent midpoints or the bisector for nonparallel lines), adjust them when the source geometry changes, and allow disassociating and reassociating them.

acceptance.sketch: Create a centerline between two parallel lines, move one line and assert the centerline moves to the new midpoint; disassociate it, move again and assert it stays put.

notes: Added from help page "About Center Marks and Centerlines"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Associative center marks and centerlines must be editable through the Properties palette, tool properties and multi-functional grips (stretch, change extension length), with system variables only affecting newly created objects.

acceptance.sketch: Change CENTERCROSSSIZE then assert an existing center mark is unchanged while a new one differs; select a center mark and use the grip to lengthen its extensions uniformly.

notes: Added from help page "About Editing Center Marks and Centerlines"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Feature control frames must be creatable with TOLERANCE or via LEADER/QLEADER options, containing a geometric characteristic symbol (form, profile, orientation, location, runout) plus tolerance data, supporting grips, editing commands, object snaps and annotative scaling.

acceptance.sketch: Run TOLERANCE with a position symbol, diameter tolerance 0.1 and datum A, assert a frame with those compartments, and verify an endpoint snap works on it.

notes: Added from help page "About Geometric Tolerances"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Composite feature control frames must allow a second row sharing the same characteristic symbol, with the pattern-level tolerance in the first row and a tighter feature-level tolerance and datums in the second, the symbol compartment spanning both rows.

acceptance.sketch: Create a frame with position symbol, 0.5 pattern tolerance on row one and 0.1 feature tolerance on row two, and assert both rows render with one merged symbol cell.

notes: Added from help page "About Composite Tolerances"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.
